species.label: Fruit fly
species.plain: The fruit fly of the laboratory, with 13,814 genes in UniProt's reference proteome. This is what the family signatures of Cells' machines find among the one protein shown for each gene.

method: The fly's proteins are the 13,814 of UniProt's gene-by-gene set of the reference proteome UP000000803 (release 2026_04): one for each gene, 3,850 with a reviewed entry and 9,964 with an unreviewed one.
Licences were read before anything was copied; each is stated in sources.
Each unit's family was taken from its own human candidates, by the same InterPro signatures that the other species' atlases ask. The build checks that the candidates carry them.

Each signature was looked for among the InterPro entries UniProt gives each protein. A unit counts as found only where a protein carries the signature of a family that makes the machine itself; an accessory family alone does not make it found.
Where no protein carries the family the engine's law names and proteins carry another family asked for the same machine (innexins, for gap junctions), the finding is 'different family'.

A product with a reviewed entry is listed as a reviewed entry, one with an unreviewed entry as a family signature. Either is a candidate by family: several units of one family (the Kv1 channels) list the same proteins, and nothing here says which protein does which unit's work.
No similarity search was run, and nothing is called an ortholog.

sources.name: UniProt
sources.cite: The UniProt Consortium, UniProt: the Universal Protein Knowledgebase in 2025, Nucleic Acids Res. 53:D609-D617 (2025)
sources.holds: the entries of the fly's proteins, reviewed and unreviewed, with the InterPro entries UniProt gives each; the signatures of the units' human candidates

sources.name: InterPro
sources.cite: Blum and others (2025) InterPro: the protein sequence classification resource in 2025. Nucleic Acids Res 53:D444-D456.
sources.holds: the identifiers and names of the family signatures

not_copied: No sequence is copied. FlyBase is linked to; nothing was downloaded from it, and the FlyBase genes used here are those UniProt gives its entries.

The fly's Shab, a voltage-gated potassium channel by its entry's name ("Potassium voltage-gated channel protein Shab"), carries the signature of another family of such channels (IPR003971, Potassium channel, voltage dependent, Kv5/Kv9) and not this one, so a search by signature does not list it.
